Test Scenario: Verify a business user can open Waste Management, KPI & APD and Energy Monitoring from the GEMS sidebar and reach the intended working pages.
Preconditions: User holds Administrator, or a role granted the relevant module menus.
Test Steps:
1. Login to GEMS.
2. In the sidebar, expand Waste Management and open each visible child (Waste Dashboard, Waste Generation, Pending Disposal, Waste Record).
3. Expand KPI & APD and open each visible child allowed for the role.
4. Expand Energy Monitoring and open Daily Electricity, Monthly Summary and Building Energy Index.
Test Data: UAT Admin or the role under test.
Expected Result: Each listed page opens without an error page. Sidebar parent labels are Waste Management, KPI & APD and Energy Monitoring. Waste children include Waste Dashboard, Waste Generation, Pending Disposal and Waste Record. KPI children include KPI / APD Summary, Monthly Evaluation, KPI History, and (Admin only) KPI Structure and PI Assignment. Energy children are Daily Electricity, Monthly Summary and Building Energy Index.
Remarks: Opening Balance, JKR Waste Reports, Waste Setup, Execute Disposal and PI Entry are implemented but hidden from the sidebar (URL / in-page links only). See GAP-WST-01 and GAP-KPA-01.

Test Scenario: Verify each M01–M03 working page shows the correct browser title and on-screen page heading so users know where they are.
Preconditions: COM-UAT-001 passed for the role under test.
Test Steps:
1. Open each page listed in Test Data.
2. Record the browser tab title and the page heading (H1).
3. Confirm no breadcrumb trail is shown.
Test Data: Waste Generation → title 'GEMS 2.0 - Waste Generation', H1 'Waste Generation'. Pending Disposal → 'GEMS 2.0 - Pending Disposal' / 'Pending Disposal'. Waste Records → 'GEMS 2.0 - Waste Records' / 'Waste Record'. Waste Dashboard → 'GEMS 2.0 - Waste Dashboard' / 'Waste Dashboard'. KPI / APD Summary → 'GEMS 2.0 - KPI / APD Dashboard' / 'KPI / APD Dashboard'. Monthly Evaluation → 'GEMS 2.0 - Monthly KPI Evaluation' / 'Monthly KPI Evaluation'. KPI History → 'GEMS 2.0 - KPI History' / 'KPI History'. Daily Electricity → 'GEMS 2.0 - Daily Electricity' / 'Daily Electricity'. Monthly Summary → 'GEMS 2.0 - Monthly Electricity Summary' / matching H1. BEI → 'GEMS 2.0 - Building Energy Index' / matching H1.
Expected Result: Every listed title and heading matches. Breadcrumb is not present (implementation gap — page title is the identifier).
Remarks: GAP-COM-01: breadcrumbs are not implemented on these pages.

Test Scenario: Verify a user can abandon an incomplete record without saving, and can return to the previous list from a detail page.
Preconditions: User can open Waste Generation and Pending Disposal.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Generation.
2. Enter a weight but do not save. Click Pending Disposal (or navigate away).
3. Return to Waste Generation and confirm the unsaved weight is cleared.
4. From Pending Disposal, open Execute Disposal on any pending row (or open Waste Generation then Pending Disposal).
5. Click Back on Execute Disposal.
Test Data: Any unsaved draft values; no save.
Expected Result: Unsaved generation is not written to Pending Disposal or Waste Records. Back from Execute Disposal returns to Pending Disposal.
Remarks: Cancel on Waste Generation is navigation, not an API cancel. Do not confuse with deleting a saved pending record (WST-UAT-009).

Test Scenario: Verify list and dashboard pages show a clear empty message when the selected premise/site and filters have no records.
Preconditions: A clean UAT premise/site with no M01–M03 transactions for the selected period, or filters that match nothing.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Generation for a premise with no recent generation — check the recent list.
2. Open Pending Disposal with Status = Pending and a date range that has none — check list and summary.
3. Open Waste Records with filters that match nothing.
4. Open Monthly Evaluation for a year with no months (or a new site).
5. Open KPI History for a year range with no evaluations.
6. Open Daily Electricity for a month with no readings.
Test Data: UAT empty site/premise; filters that return zero rows.
Expected Result: Pages do not crash. User sees the implemented empty text, including: 'No generation records yet.'; 'No pending disposal records.' / 'Nothing is pending disposal'; 'No waste records yet.' or 'No records match the current filters.'; 'No evaluation months yet.'; 'No evaluation months in the selected range.'; daily grid still renders calendar days with blank consumption (not invented zeros) when no readings exist.
Remarks: Empty daily energy days show em-dash, not 0.00. Monthly energy table may show 0.00 for a meter with no data — see GAP-ENR-01.

Test Scenario: Verify mandatory-field and success messages are shown in business language (not a blank failure) when a user saves incorrectly and when a save succeeds.
Preconditions: User can create waste generation and PI entry (or Admin can).
Test Steps:
1. On Waste Generation, click Save with waste type and weight blank.
2. Fill valid data and Save.
3. On a PI Entry page (Admin), click Submit with a required parameter blank.
4. Enter a valid value, Save Draft, then observe the success notification.
Test Data: Blank mandatory fields; then valid WST-GEN-01 data / a valid PI parameter.
Expected Result: Incomplete save is blocked and a readable warning is shown (Waste: 'Select a waste type.' / 'Enter a waste weight greater than zero.'). Successful generation shows 'Waste generation recorded and is now pending collection.' PI submit without a required value shows 'Enter a value for "{parameter label}" before submitting.' Successful PI save/submit shows the corresponding success notification.
Remarks: Record the exact on-screen wording. Generic 'Something went wrong' is a fail.

Test Scenario: Verify a saved business record is still present after browser refresh and after leaving the module and returning.
Preconditions: WST-UAT-001 or equivalent saved generation exists.
Test Steps:
1. Save a waste generation (or use WST-GEN-01).
2. Refresh the browser on Waste Generation.
3. Open Pending Disposal and find the record.
4. Logout, login again, and search the same record.
Expected Result: The same waste reference, premise, waste type, date and weight are still shown. The record was not duplicated by refresh.
Remarks: If refresh creates a second record, fail as duplicate-submit defect.

Test Scenario: Verify a user with no Waste, KPI or Energy role cannot open those modules from the sidebar, and a direct URL does not allow them to change data.
Preconditions: A GEMS user exists who is not Administrator, Waste User/Officer, KPI Admin/PI Entry/KPI Viewer, Utility Reader or KPI Admin.
Test Steps:
1. Login as the unauthorised user.
2. Confirm Waste Management, KPI & APD and Energy Monitoring are not in the sidebar.
3. Paste a direct URL for p_waste_generation, p_kpa_structure and p_energy_daily.
4. Attempt to save if the page renders.
Expected Result: Sidebar does not show the three modules. Direct URL either redirects, shows an access message, or the save is rejected with 'You are not allowed to create or change waste records.' / 'You are not allowed to change the KPI structure.' / 'You are not allowed to record meter readings.' No new official record is created.
Remarks: Account list is TBC. Do not use this case to test general GEMS user administration screens.

Test Scenario: Verify dates and quantities display in a consistent business format so dashboard, lists and forms can be reconciled.
Preconditions: At least one waste generation in kg with 3 decimal places and one energy reading with 2 decimal places exist.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Generation / Pending Disposal / Dashboard for the test record.
2. Confirm weight is shown in kg (3 decimal places where entered).
3. Open Daily Electricity and confirm cumulative/consumption use 2 decimal places.
4. Open KPI summary and confirm APD amounts are in RM with 2 decimal places.
Test Data: WST-GEN-02 (12.500 kg); ENR daily reading 10000.00; any KPI month with APD figures.
Expected Result: Waste quantities are kg on generation/pending (not silently converted to MT on those screens). Energy kWh shows 2 decimals. APD shows 2 decimals. Dates use the date picker / ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) on forms and a readable date on lists. 1 MT = 1,000 kg is stated on the waste dashboard unit note.
Remarks: Fifth Schedule Waste Record form still uses MT or kg — do not treat that as a generation-screen defect.

Test Scenario: Verify a facility officer can record scheduled waste generated at a premise and that the record is accepted into the official register.
Preconditions: Tester is logged in with a Waste User, Waste Officer or Administrator account that can see Waste Management. Dedicated UAT premise (UAT Premise A) is selected. At least one active scheduled waste type is available for that premise (prefer SW410 if listed). Do not use a live operational premise.
Test Steps:
1. Login to GEMS.
2. Open Waste Management > Waste Generation.
3. Select UAT Premise A.
4. Select waste type SW410 (or the agreed UAT waste type).
5. Enter waste weight 50.000 kg.
6. Set Date to 15/09/2026 (or today if 15/09/2026 is in the future on the test day).
7. Enter remarks 'UAT WST-GEN-01'.
8. Save.
9. Record the waste reference shown in the recent list.
Test Data: Premise: UAT Premise A. Waste type: SW410. Weight: 50.000 kg. Date: 15/09/2026 (or today). Remarks: UAT WST-GEN-01. Capture system reference as WST-REF-01.
Expected Result: Save succeeds. Notification: 'Waste generation recorded and is now pending collection.' Recent list shows the new row with matching waste type, date, registered weight 50.000 kg and status Pending Collection. A waste reference is allocated. Record is FINAL in the official register (it counts toward balance).
Remarks: Generation saves immediately as Final + Pending Collection. There is no draft and no approval step. Date cannot be future — if UAT runs before 15/09/2026 use today and record the actual date used.

Test Scenario: Verify waste generation cannot be saved when mandatory business information is missing.
Preconditions: Tester is logged in with a Waste User, Waste Officer or Administrator account that can see Waste Management. Dedicated UAT premise (UAT Premise A) is selected. At least one active scheduled waste type is available for that premise (prefer SW410 if listed). Do not use a live operational premise.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Generation.
2. Clear or leave Waste type unselected, leave Waste weight blank, and clear Date if possible.
3. Attempt Save.
4. Select a waste type only, leave weight blank, attempt Save.
5. Enter weight 50.000 and leave waste type blank, attempt Save.
Test Data: Blank waste type; blank weight; blank date.
Expected Result: No new pending record is created. User is shown the implemented messages: 'Select a waste type.'; 'Enter a waste weight greater than zero.'; 'Enter the waste generation date.' as applicable.
Remarks: Mandatory fields on this screen: Premise, Waste type, Waste weight (kg), Date. Remarks are optional.

Test Scenario: Verify a facility officer cannot record a zero or negative generated weight.
Preconditions: Tester is logged in with a Waste User, Waste Officer or Administrator account that can see Waste Management. Dedicated UAT premise (UAT Premise A) is selected. At least one active scheduled waste type is available for that premise (prefer SW410 if listed). Do not use a live operational premise.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Generation and select UAT Premise A and SW410.
2. Enter weight 0 and a valid date. Save.
3. Enter weight -10. Save.
4. Enter weight 50.000 and Save to confirm the form still works afterwards.
Test Data: Weight 0; weight -10; then valid 50.000 kg (discard or cancel this extra row if created — or use it as WST-GEN-extra).
Expected Result: 0 and -10 are rejected. Message includes 'Enter a waste weight greater than zero.' No official pending row is created for the invalid attempts.
Remarks: Minimum accepted weight is 0.001 kg.

Test Scenario: Verify generated waste cannot be backdated into the future.
Preconditions: Tester is logged in with a Waste User, Waste Officer or Administrator account that can see Waste Management. Dedicated UAT premise (UAT Premise A) is selected. At least one active scheduled waste type is available for that premise (prefer SW410 if listed). Do not use a live operational premise.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Generation.
2. Select premise and waste type.
3. Enter weight 10.000 kg.
4. Set Date to tomorrow. Save.
Expected Result: Save is rejected. Message: 'The waste generation date cannot be in the future.' No pending record is created.
Remarks: Date control also has max = today.

Test Scenario: Verify a decimal scheduled-waste quantity can be recorded and displayed at gram precision.
Preconditions: Tester is logged in with a Waste User, Waste Officer or Administrator account that can see Waste Management. Dedicated UAT premise (UAT Premise A) is selected. At least one active scheduled waste type is available for that premise (prefer SW410 if listed). Do not use a live operational premise.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Generation.
2. Select UAT Premise A and SW410.
3. Enter 12.500 kg, date today, remarks 'UAT WST-GEN-02'.
4. Save.
5. Confirm the recent list and Pending Disposal show 12.500 kg.
Test Data: WST-GEN-02: 12.500 kg, today, SW410, remarks UAT WST-GEN-02. Capture reference WST-REF-02.
Expected Result: Record saves. Registered weight displays as 12.500 kg on Generation recent list and Pending Disposal. Balance increases by 12.500 kg (not rounded to a whole kilogram).
Remarks: Use this row later only if isolation is still clean; otherwise cancel it after the check.

Test Scenario: Verify newly generated scheduled waste appears in Pending Disposal with the correct premise, waste code and outstanding weight.
Preconditions: WST-UAT-001 completed. WST-REF-01 known.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Management > Pending Disposal.
2. Select UAT Premise A.
3. Set Status to Pending.
4. Search using the waste reference from WST-UAT-001.
5. Read the row and the Pending by waste-type summary.
Test Data: WST-REF-01; 50.000 kg; SW410; UAT Premise A.
Expected Result: The row is listed. Waste type / SW code matches SW410. Generated date matches. Registered (kg) = 50.000. Disposed (kg) is blank or 0. Status badge = Pending Collection. Pending Weight KPI includes this 50.000 kg. Summary table shows SW410 with pending kg including 50.000.
Remarks: Screen title is Pending Disposal; status text is Pending Collection. Both are correct implemented labels.

Test Scenario: Verify several generation records for the same premise remain separate and the pending weight is the sum of outstanding rows.
Preconditions: WST-REF-01 (50.000 kg) and WST-REF-02 (12.500 kg) both still Pending for the same premise and waste type. No other pending SW410 on that premise, or tester records the before/after totals.
Test Steps:
1. Note Pending Weight and SW410 summary kg before this check (or immediately after creating the two rows).
2. Confirm both references appear as separate rows.
3. Add the registered kg of all pending SW410 rows and compare with the SW410 summary Pending (kg) and the Pending Weight card.
Test Data: WST-REF-01 50.000 + WST-REF-02 12.500 = 62.500 kg (if only these two pending SW410 rows).
Expected Result: Each generation remains its own row with its own reference. Pending Weight and SW410 Pending (kg) equal the sum of pending registered weights for that filter (62.500 kg if only these two).
Remarks: If other pending rows exist, reconcile against the full filtered list — do not force 62.500.

Test Scenario: Verify a pending generation can be corrected (waste type, weight, date, remarks) before collection.
Preconditions: A dedicated pending row exists (create WST-GEN-03: 20.000 kg, remarks UAT-EDIT-BEFORE) that will not be used in the 100/50/30 balance case.
Test Steps:
1. Open Pending Disposal.
2. On the dedicated pending row, click Edit.
3. Change weight to 25.000 kg, date if needed, remarks to 'UAT-EDIT-AFTER'.
4. Save.
5. Re-open the row / refresh the list.
Test Data: Before: 20.000 kg. After: 25.000 kg, remarks UAT-EDIT-AFTER. Optional correction reason.
Expected Result: Save succeeds. List shows 25.000 kg and updated remarks. Pending summary kg increases by 5.000 versus the pre-edit value. Status remains Pending Collection. Official balance uses 25.000 kg, not 20.000 kg.
Remarks: Edit is allowed only while Pending. After disposal the generation weight is locked.

Test Scenario: Verify a pending generation can be cancelled so it leaves the collection queue and no longer affects the premise balance, while remaining on the audit trail.
Preconditions: A dedicated pending row exists that is not part of the official E2E transaction (create WST-GEN-04: 8.000 kg if needed).
Test Steps:
1. Note Current Balance / pending kg for the waste type.
2. On the dedicated row, click Delete.
3. Leave reason blank and confirm — expect block.
4. Enter reason 'UAT cancel pending — not collected'.
5. Confirm delete.
6. Refresh Pending Disposal (Status Pending and Status All).
7. Open Waste Records and search the reference.
Test Data: Reason required: 'UAT cancel pending — not collected'. Weight 8.000 kg.
Expected Result: Blank reason is rejected: 'Enter the reason for deleting this pending waste record.' After confirm, row disappears from Pending. Modal text advised the row is cancelled and kept for audit. Waste Records / Status All can still find it as cancelled / not pending. Premise balance no longer includes the 8.000 kg. Notification confirms the cancel.
Remarks: The row is not physically removed. Cancelled and Draft records are excluded from official totals.

Test Scenario: Verify a facility officer can record a full collection/disposal equal to the registered weight, with both mandatory disposal photographs.
Preconditions: A pending generation exists for full disposal (create WST-GEN-05: 40.000 kg, date today, remarks UAT-FULL-DISP). Two image files are available.
Test Steps:
1. Open Pending Disposal and find WST-GEN-05.
2. Click Execute disposal.
3. Confirm Section A shows the same reference, waste type, generated date, 40.000 kg and premise.
4. Attach During disposal image and After disposal image.
5. Set Disposal date = today (on or after generated date).
6. Enter Actual disposed weight 40.000 kg.
7. Save.
8. Return to Pending Disposal, Status = Pending, then Status = Disposed.
Test Data: WST-GEN-05: registered 40.000 kg; actual 40.000 kg; two JPG/PNG images; disposal date = today.
Expected Result: Save succeeds. Message: 'Disposal recorded. The waste record is now marked as Disposed.' User is returned to Pending Disposal. Row is no longer Pending Collection. Status = Disposed. Disposed (kg) = 40.000. A linked disposal transaction exists. Official balance decreases by 40.000 kg.
Remarks: There is no approval step. One disposal per generation record.

Test Scenario: Verify disposal cannot be completed without both during and after photographs.
Preconditions: A pending generation exists (create WST-GEN-06: 5.000 kg if needed).
Test Steps:
1. Open Execute Disposal for the pending row.
2. Enter disposal date and actual weight 5.000 kg but attach no images. Attempt Save.
3. Attach only the During image. Attempt Save.
4. Attach only the After image (remove During if needed). Attempt Save.
Expected Result: Save remains blocked or is rejected. Messages: 'Attach the during disposal image before saving.' and/or 'Attach the after disposal image before saving.' Record stays Pending Collection. No disposal transaction is created.
Remarks: Save control is disabled until both images are attached.

Test Scenario: Verify disposal date cannot be in the future and cannot be earlier than the generation date.
Preconditions: Pending generation dated today or a known past date (use WST-GEN-06 if still pending).
Test Steps:
1. Open Execute Disposal.
2. Attach both images.
3. Set disposal date to tomorrow, actual weight equal to registered. Save.
4. Set disposal date to one day before the generated date. Save.
5. Set disposal date = generated date (or today). Do not save if this would consume the E2E row — cancel out after the messages are confirmed, or use a disposable pending row.
Test Data: Future date; date before generation; valid date = generated date.
Expected Result: Future date rejected: 'The disposal date cannot be in the future.' Earlier-than-generation rejected: 'The disposal date cannot be earlier than the generation date.' Record remains pending until a valid save.
Remarks: Use a disposable pending row so the E2E 50 kg row is not accidentally disposed here.

Test Scenario: Verify a disposal that would take more scheduled waste than the premise holds is rejected.
Preconditions: Known current balance for UAT Premise A + SW410 (from Dashboard Current Balance or Opening + net). A pending generation exists.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Dashboard, filter premise + SW410, note Current Balance (kg).
2. Open Execute Disposal on a pending SW410 row.
3. Attach both images.
4. Enter Actual disposed weight = Current Balance + 100 kg.
5. Save.
Test Data: Actual qty = current SW410 balance + 100 kg.
Expected Result: Save is rejected. Message: 'Disposal quantity is not supported by the available balance for this event date. Review the quantity and earlier waste records.' Generation remains Pending Collection. Balance unchanged.
Remarks: Actual disposed may exceed the registered weight of this one row if the premise holds enough of that SW code (opening + earlier production). This test uses an amount larger than the whole premise balance.

Test Scenario: Verify a short collection (actual disposed less than registered) marks the generation as Disposed and leaves the remainder in the premise balance — not as a new pending row.
Preconditions: Use the official E2E generation WST-REF-01 (50.000 kg) only if the controlled balance case is being executed now; otherwise create WST-GEN-07: 50.000 kg pending.
Test Steps:
1. Note Current Balance for the premise + SW code.
2. Execute disposal on the 50.000 kg pending row.
3. Attach both images.
4. Disposal date today.
5. Actual disposed weight 30.000 kg.
6. Save.
7. Open Pending Disposal Status = Pending and search the reference.
8. Switch Status to Disposed and find the reference.
9. Recalculate Current Balance.
Test Data: Registered 50.000 kg. Actual disposed 30.000 kg. Remainder 20.000 kg.
Expected Result: Disposal saves. Generation status becomes Disposed (not left Pending). No second pending row is created for the 20.000 kg shortfall. Registered weight on the produced record remains 50.000 kg. Disposed (kg) on the list = 30.000. Premise current balance decreases by 30.000 kg only (remainder 20.000 kg stays in stock). Screen may note that the remainder stays in the premise balance.
Remarks: This is the implemented partial-disposal rule. Do not expect a split pending record. One disposal per generation — the 20 kg cannot be disposed against the same generation again.

Test Scenario: Verify consignment note and receipt are optional and can be stored with reference numbers when provided.
Preconditions: A disposable pending row exists (create WST-GEN-08: 6.000 kg). Optional PDF/JPG files available.
Test Steps:
1. Execute disposal.
2. Attach both mandatory images.
3. Attach a consignment note and enter reference 'CN-UAT-001'.
4. Attach a consignment receipt and enter reference 'CR-UAT-001'.
5. Enter actual = registered. Save.
6. Open the record from Waste Records / View and confirm the documents and references are visible.
Test Data: CN-UAT-001; CR-UAT-001; two evidence images; optional note/receipt files.
Expected Result: Disposal succeeds with or without consignment files. When provided, the files and reference numbers are stored on the disposal record and can be seen when the record is opened.
Remarks: Consignment documents are optional. Evidence images are not.

Test Scenario: Verify a generation that has already been disposed cannot be disposed a second time.
Preconditions: WST-UAT-010 or WST-UAT-014 already disposed a row. Tester has that reference.
Test Steps:
1. Open Pending Disposal, Status = Disposed, find the disposed reference.
2. Confirm Execute disposal is not offered (or open p_waste_dispose?id= of that record if the action is hidden).
3. If the page opens, attempt to save another disposal.
Test Data: Already-disposed reference from WST-GEN-05 or WST-REF-01.
Expected Result: Execute disposal is not available for Disposed rows. If the URL is opened, the system states 'This waste record is already disposed and can no longer be changed.' No second disposal transaction is created.
Remarks: Remainder after a short collection is not disposed through the same generation row.

Test Scenario: Verify a user can find historical waste transactions by reference, date, waste type, premise and status.
Preconditions: WST-REF-01 and at least one disposed record exist.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Management > Waste Record.
2. Search the waste reference from the E2E generation.
3. Filter premise = UAT Premise A, waste type = SW410, date from/to covering 15/09/2026.
4. Filter type Produced, then Disposed.
5. Filter status Final.
6. Open (View) the produced row and the disposed row.
Test Data: WST-REF-01; UAT Premise A; SW410; period covering the test dates.
Expected Result: Search returns the matching row(s). Filters reduce the list to matching premise, SW code, dates, type and status. View shows the same reference, dates, quantities and, for the lifecycle pair, the linked generation/disposal panel. Final produced and final disposed rows are both listed. Cancelled rows do not appear as Final.
Remarks: Waste Record is the list. The Fifth Schedule form is the view/edit page and is not in the sidebar.

Test Scenario: Verify a Waste Officer / Administrator can record the starting quantity held at a premise so later generation and disposal can be reconciled.
Preconditions: Logged in as Waste Officer or Administrator. Page is reached via URL p_waste_opening_balance (not in the sidebar). Prefer a waste type reserved for the controlled balance case, or perform this BEFORE other SW410 movements on a clean UAT premise.
Test Steps:
1. Open p_waste_opening_balance.
2. Add / save opening balance.
3. Select UAT Premise A, SW410, as-at date 31/08/2026, quantity 100, unit kg.
4. Save.
5. Refresh the opening-balance list.
6. Open Waste Dashboard for September 2026, same premise and SW410, and read Opening Balance.
Test Data: UAT-OB-01: Premise UAT Premise A; SW410; as-at 31/08/2026; 100.000 kg.
Expected Result: Save succeeds. List shows 100.000 kg as at 31/08/2026. Dashboard Opening Balance for September 2026 = 100.000 kg (if no Final movements after 31/08/2026 and before 01/09/2026). Opening is not listed as Produced.
Remarks: GAP-WST-01: Opening Balance is hidden from the sidebar. Zero is allowed; negative is not. One opening row per premise + SW code (save updates the same row).

Test Scenario: Verify current scheduled-waste balance equals Opening + Generated − Disposed using a controlled dataset.
Preconditions: Clean UAT Premise A + SW410 for the period, or tester records any extra Final SW410 movements and includes them. Recommended controlled set: Opening 100.000 kg (WST-UAT-018); Generated 50.000 kg (WST-REF-01); Disposed actual 30.000 kg (WST-UAT-014). WST-REF-02 and other extras must be cancelled or excluded from this SW code.
Test Steps:
1. Confirm opening 100.000 kg as at 31/08/2026.
2. Confirm one Final produced 50.000 kg in September.
3. Confirm one Final disposed 30.000 kg in September.
4. Manually calculate 100 + 50 − 30 = 120.
5. Open Waste Dashboard, month September 2026, premise UAT Premise A, SW410.
6. Read Opening, Produced, Disposed, Current Balance.
7. Open the balance table row for that premise + SW410.
Test Data: Opening 100.000 kg. Produced 50.000 kg. Disposed 30.000 kg. Expected closing / current = 120.000 kg. Net movement = 20.000 kg.
Expected Result: Dashboard Opening = 100.000 kg. Produced = 50.000 kg. Disposed = 30.000 kg. Net Movement = 20.000 kg. Current Balance / Closing = 120.000 kg. Balance table Opening + Produced − Disposed = Closing. Cancelled rows (if any) are excluded. Units kg; 120.000 kg = 0.120 MT if MT is also shown.
Remarks: Formula (implemented): Current = Opening kg + sum(Final Produced kg) − sum(Final Disposed kg), with opening applied as the starting point and only Final rows after the opening as-at date. Draft and Cancelled are excluded. If extra rows exist, replace 120 with the testers' own controlled arithmetic and attach the working.

Test Scenario: Verify every dashboard figure for the controlled period can be traced to the underlying waste transactions.
Preconditions: Same controlled September 2026 / UAT Premise A / SW410 dataset as WST-UAT-019. Other premises may exist — filter to the UAT premise.
Test Steps:
1. Open Waste Dashboard.
2. Set Month = September, Year = 2026, Premise = UAT Premise A, Waste type = SW410.
3. Copy Opening, Produced, Disposed, Net Movement, Current Balance, Final Transactions, Pending Disposal kg.
4. Open Waste Records with the same premise, SW code and September dates, Status Final — sum Produced and Disposed kg.
5. Open Pending Disposal Status = Pending for that premise/SW — sum registered kg.
6. Click the Pending Disposal KPI and confirm it opens the pending page.
7. Review Produced/Disposed/Pending/Closing by SW and by premise tables.
Test Data: Expected (isolated SW410): Opening 100.000; Produced 50.000; Disposed 30.000; Net 20.000; Current 120.000; Final Transactions = 2 (one Produced + one Disposed) if no other Final SW410 rows; Pending Disposal kg = 0 after WST-UAT-014.
Expected Result: Each KPI equals the independently summed source records for the same filter. Pending Disposal kg is the current pending collection total (not limited to the selected month — if this differs from 0 because of other pending rows, record the actual pending list). Click-through opens Waste Records or Pending Disposal with the filter applied. Presence of a number without reconciliation is a fail.
Remarks: Pending Disposal kg and pending-by-SW are current outstanding, not period-bound. Draft count on the dashboard is all drafts, not period-bound. Record as observation if that surprises the business (GAP-WST-03).

Test Scenario: Verify a Waste Officer / Administrator can generate a JKR scheduled-waste report version for a premise and period and open the PDF and Excel files.
Preconditions: Logged in as Waste Officer or Administrator. Page via URL p_waste_report (not in the sidebar). Controlled September data exists.
Test Steps:
1. Open p_waste_report.
2. Click Generate.

Test Scenario: Verify Dataset A (normal / meeting target) — PI 1A, 1E and 4C calculate achievement, pass and APD exactly as the engine defines.

2. Open PI 1E. Enter p1=10, p2=10, p3=5, p4=5, p5=0, p6=0. Save. Record results.

Test Data:
APD Maximum RM 207,356.03.

PI 1A EXPRESSION (p1/p2)*100: 88/100*100 = 88.0000%. Target 80, GTE → PASS. Weight 5%. APD exposure = round(207356.03*5/100,2) = 10,367.80. Deducted 0.00. Demerit 0.

PI 1E BACKLOG_AVG: buckets (10/10)=100, (5/5)=100, (0/0 treated as no backlog)=100. Mean 100.0000%. Target 100 → PASS. Exposure 10,367.80. Deducted 0.00.

PI 4C AVG_PARAMS: mean(100,100)=100.0000%. Target 100 → PASS. Weight 3%. Exposure = round(207356.03*3/100,2) = 6,220.68. Deducted 0.00.
Expected Result: System achievement, pass text (Target met), APD exposure and APD deducted match the manual working to 4 decimal places on achievement and 2 decimal places on RM. Month totals do not include APD for these three PIs.
Remarks: Achievement is rounded to 4 decimal places. APD is rounded to 2 decimal places. A bucket with total 0 on PI 1E scores 100%.

Test Scenario: Verify Dataset B (boundary / exactly on target) — PI 1A at 80%, PI 3B BEI exactly 170.6500, and PI 3C with zero wastage findings.

Test Scenario: Verify BEI is calculated as (electricity + chilled water) / gross floor area × annualisation factor, and that a value at or below target is a pass.
Preconditions: UAT Site A. Incoming No.1 September total 375.00 kWh. Incoming No.2 unused (0). Tester can save site configuration.
Test Steps:
1. Open Energy Monitoring > Building Energy Index.
2. Select UAT Site A, Year 2026.
3. Set Gross floor area 10,000 m², Target BEI 170.65, Annualisation factor 12. Save configuration.
4. On September, leave Electricity as the derived 375.00 (or type it if not prefilled).
5. Enter Chilled water 125.00.
6. Save the month if required and read Actual BEI, result and pass/fail.
Test Data: Electricity 375.00. Chilled 125.00. Total energy 500.00. GFA 10,000. Factor 12. Manual BEI = (500 / 10000) × 12 = 0.6000. Target 170.65. 0.6000 ≤ 170.65 → PASS. Result % = 100.
Expected Result: Electricity defaults from daily readings (375.00) with hint 'From daily readings'. Total energy 500.00. Actual BEI 0.6000. Month passes. Result 100%. Configuration save: 'Energy configuration saved.' Month save: 'Monthly BEI saved.'
Remarks: Implemented formula: actualBei = round((electricityKwh + chilledWaterKwh) / floorAreaSqm × factor, 4); pass when actualBei <= targetBei + 0.00005. Factor 12 is required when the consumption is a monthly figure and the target is an annual BEI.

Expected Result: Actual BEI 1800.0000. Target not met / 0%. Status Draft until finalised. September row is still 0.6000 / 100%. Year cards count October as failing and September as passing.

Test Scenario: Verify BEI cannot be scored when gross floor area is missing / not set, and the user is told to enter it.

Test Scenario: Verify a zero or negative floor area is rejected or produces no BEI, and a zero/negative target prevents scoring.

Test Scenario: Verify typing over the electricity figure marks the month as an override, and clearing it returns the value derived from daily readings.
